name: Onyx Settings
description: Connection to ONYX, our self-hosted AI at ai.naarni.com. Nothing here changes what the platform records — AI only rewrites text that has already been captured, and every feature that uses it keeps working when this is off.

fields.label: Enabled
fields.description: Off by default. With this off, every AI-assisted feature falls back to its plain deterministic output instead of failing.

fields.label: Base URL
fields.description: Host only. The /api prefix is added automatically.

fields.label: API Key or Token
fields.description: Either an ONYX API key (on_...) or a personal access token (onyx_pat_...). Prefer an API key created for this integration alone: a personal token carries one person's identity and dies with their account. Making days searchable in ONYX additionally needs curator rights, which a scoped token will not have.

fields.label: Assistant ID
fields.description: 0 is the ONYX default assistant. Every call disables tools and search, so the assistant acts as a plain language model — the instructions come from this app, not from the assistant's prompt.

fields.label: Timeout (seconds)
fields.description: Calls only ever run in background jobs, never in a request a person is waiting on.

fields.label: API Path Prefix
fields.description: Leave as /api unless the ONYX ingress is configured to serve the backend at the root.

fields.label: How this is used
fields.default: ONYX cannot guarantee JSON output on its chat endpoint, so every caller validates the reply and falls back to a plain rendering if it does not parse. After three consecutive failures the client stops calling for 15 minutes and everything runs on the fallback.
